profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, traded under the ticker CRNC and registered with the SEC under CIK 0001768267. On its own site the company describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, powered by CaLLM, which it describes as its family of language models for natural, multimodal and safe interactions. It lists the Cerence SDK V9 for on-device voice AI with modular APIs and enterprise-ready security, and describes AI Box architectures for agentic in-car experiences at the edge without disrupting existing infotainment platforms.

The site reports second quarter fiscal year 2026 results including $64.2 million in revenue, $7.2 million in Adjusted EBITDA, net income of $1.7 million, $14.1 million in operating cash flow and $13.6 million in free cash flow, and says it raised the midpoints of full-year revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance. It states that Cerence xUI-powered vehicles have started production and that adoption of Audio AI and generative AI solutions is expanding with global OEMs. The company says it received the ECARX 2026 Quality Pioneer Award at ECARX's Global Partner Conference for the third consecutive year, and describes a partnership with ECARX dating to 2017 covering multilingual speech recognition, AI-powered voice assistants and intelligent cockpit experiences across GEELY brands including Proton, smart Automobile, Group Lotus and Lynk & Co. It also describes a partnership with Code Factory S.L. on VoiceLaier, an embedded voice AI solution for self-service kiosks, and says its text-to-speech product includes machine-readable metadata and digital audio watermarking built for the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) transparency requirements for synthetic audio, with obligations expected to apply from August 2, 2026.

The site also covers agentic AI in industrial settings following HANNOVER MESSE 2026 and a Q&A with Markus Funk, its Director of User Experience, on AI-driven design workflows. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
